subject: research/chip-toolchain
professional: a senior digital design / EDA engineer who runs open synthesis flows (Yosys + ABC) and signs off RTL with simulation and formal equivalence. First checks: do the synthesised netlists compute the right function, are the gate counts a property of the design or of the script, does the equivalence wrapper distinguish 'not equivalent' from 'tool failed', and do the sequential testbenches cover the corner cases (full, empty, underflow)

evidence.correctness: Installed the same Ubuntu 24.04 packages the README names (yosys 0.33-5build2, iverilog 12.0-2build2, verilator 5.020-1; about 47 MB, not a large toolchain). experiments/run.py reproduces experiments/results.txt byte-for-byte in 2.0 s (diff empty), and figure.py regenerates cells_vs_width.svg identically in a scratch copy. Independent recomputations: (1) the synthesised mult_op netlists (write_verilog after the README's flow) simulated in Icarus against Verilog i*j for all 256 (W=4) and all 65,536 (W=8) input pairs: 0 mismatches. (2) The negative control adder_bug at W=8 simulated exhaustively: 28,672 of 65,536 sums wrong, exactly the analytic count (pairs whose low 3 bits carry out of bit 2: 28/64 of all pairs), and 4+4 gives 0, so the SAT 'False' is a real non-equivalence, not a tool error. (3) A hand-built 4-bit ripple adder in the same gate library (XOR sum, AND for bit 0, MUX carry) is 11 cells, path length 4 by ltp, and is SAT-proved equal to adder_ripple; textbook count 3W-1. The flow's 17 cells / depth 7 (5W-3 / 2W-1) are therefore what this ABC script produces, about 55% above a trivially available netlist, not the cost of a ripple adder. (4) The FIFO's 40/75 flops decomposed with stat: 32/64 DFFE memory bits, 6/8 SDFFE pointer bits, and 2/3 extra SDFF bits that drive the read-mux select (a registered copy of the next read address created by memory mapping), so the 'extra' is AW bits of read address, not the write address the README guesses.
evidence.completeness: Every README item runs end to end: 8 unit tests OK in 1.3 s (README: '8 tests, about 2 s'), results table, equivalence (W=4/8/12 True, bug False), lint (UNOPTFLAT on adder_ripple only), 256-vector simulation, the SVG. Limits (no OpenROAD, PDK, cocotb, liberty) are stated, not claimed. No stubs. Live page https://marisstella.app/research/chip-toolchain/ not loaded (proxy 403), not scored.
evidence.verification: python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests: 8 tests OK (they skip silently without the tools). Five seeded mutants via quality_mutate.py: 3 caught (dropping sat -verify, removing the adder_bug fault, inverting the FIFO full flag's MSB compare), 2 survived: removing the FIFO's '!empty' underflow guard on pop (tb_fifo never pops while empty and observes the result), and dropping MUX from the ABC gate library (no test pins any cell count; the flop test is only a >= 38 lower bound). The equivalence test cannot tell a tool error from a non-equivalence (see craft).
evidence.craft: Read flow.py (83 lines), run.py, figure.py, tests/test_flow.py and all seven .v files. Small and readable, but: flow.py:83 equivalent() returns p.returncode == 0, so a missing file, wrong top name or misspelled parameter all return False, the same as a proved non-equivalence (ran: equivalent('nope.v',...), wrong top, chparam WW, all False). In an equivalence wrapper whose negative control is the headline check this is a silent failure. synth_stats returns depth None silently if ltp output does not parse. run.py:44 'lines = vecs' is dead aliasing. synth already runs ABC, then abc -g remaps a second time (undocumented double mapping).
evidence.claims: Checked against results.txt and the rerun: versions, every table cell, 5W-3 and 2W-1 at W=4..32, '0, 1, 5 and 13 more cells', equivalence results, lint results, 256 vectors 0 mismatches, 40 vs 38 flops: all pass. Partial: README:32 'The ripple adder costs 5W-3 cells ... and depth 2W-1' reads as a property of the adder; it is the script's output (hand netlist 3W-1, depth W). README:36 speculates the extra flops are the write address; they are the read address. ABC (Brayton and Mishchenko, CAV 2010) is used but not cited in 'Builds on'. AI assistance disclosed; OpenROAD absence disclosed prominently.
evidence.fitness: It is milestone-1 infrastructure: a recorded, reproducible Yosys/Icarus/Verilator setup that later projects in this repo build on (chip-abc-sweep, chip-rtl-loop, chip-pnr, eda-harness cite it). As research there is no result: these are standard smoke flows (Yosys synth+abc, Yosys miter/sat, the same steps OpenLane/OpenROAD-flow-scripts automate) on five toy designs with one script and one version, no baseline beyond the tool itself, and the one interesting observation (ABC with -g leaves a ripple adder ~55% larger than a hand netlist using the MUX it was offered) is not noticed. Far from the research brief's PhD/publishable bar on its own, as it was meant to be.
evidence.domain: Method is standard practice for an open front end (miter + SAT for combinational equivalence, exhaustive simulation for a 4-bit adder, Verilator lint). Departures a design engineer would flag: gate counts reported without noting the script is not area-optimal or delay-targeted (no abc -D, no dch/resyn2 comparison here; chip-abc-sweep does that later); the sequential FIFO has no formal property check (e.g. SymbiYosys) and its testbench omits underflow and simultaneous push/pop; equivalence is only combinational, which is all these designs need.

defects.what: equivalent() returns p.returncode == 0, so any Yosys error (missing file, wrong top, misspelled chparam) returns False, indistinguishable from a proved non-equivalence. The negative-control check would pass on a broken flow. Should raise on errors and only return False when sat reports a counterexample.

The FIFO testbench never observes a pop while empty: removing the '!empty' underflow guard (fifo.v:18) leaves all tests green. README:34 says FIFO behaviour is 'checked in the unit tests'; underflow and simultaneous push/pop are not.
No test pins any reported cell count (flops only >= 38), so changing the ABC gate library (dropping MUX) or the script leaves every test green while the README table would change.

'The ripple adder costs 5W-3 cells ... and depth 2W-1' states a script artifact as the adder's cost. A hand netlist in the same library (MUX carry) is 3W-1 cells and depth W (11 cells, path 4 at W=4, SAT-proved equal); the flow's ABC pass leaves it about 55% larger and the README does not notice.

The extra FIFO flops are guessed to be 'the 2-bit write address'; stat/write_verilog show they are an AW-bit register driving the read mux select (read address), 2 at AW=2 and 3 at AW=3 (75 = 64 + 8 + 3, also unexplained in the README).
ABC does all technology mapping but is not cited in 'Builds on' (Brayton and Mishchenko, CAV 2010, doi:10.1007/978-3-642-14295-6_5, already cited by sibling research/chip-abc-sweep).
Dead aliasing 'lines = vecs'; synth_stats silently returns depth None if ltp output does not parse (flow.py:54).

verdict: A small, honest, fully reproducible toolchain milestone: with the README's own apt packages, results.txt and the SVG regenerate byte-for-byte and the 8 tests pass. Independent checks agree on function: the synthesised multipliers are exhaustively correct at W=4 and 8 and the negative control fails on exactly the analytic 28,672 of 65,536 inputs. It misses the bar on verification (2 of 5 seeded bugs survive, including the FIFO underflow guard) and on craft, because the equivalence wrapper reports any tool error as 'not equivalent', which is a silent failure for the check the milestone is meant to establish. The headline '5W-3 cells, depth 2W-1' is the ABC script's output, not a ripple adder's cost (a hand netlist is 3W-1 cells, depth W), and the README's guess about the extra FIFO flops names the wrong pointer. As research it is infrastructure with no new result, appropriate for a first milestone, far from the publishable bar on its own.
